2608.20204.title: ContractScrub: A benchmark for final review of legal contracts
2608.20204.paper_summary: Legal work, with its heavy reliance on processing large amounts of text, is often considered one of the domains most exposed to the use of LLMs. Contract ``scrubbing,'' the final review of transactional agreements for errors and inconsistencies, is a particularly suitable task for automation, because it is routine, painstaking work requiring detailed attention to long documents. Scrubbing also seems to align naturally with the general capabilities expected of frontier LLMs around long-context reasoning, consistency checking, and named entity recognition (NER). Despite the economic value and potential for automation, no formal evaluations of LLMs performing contract scrubbing have been conducted. We introduce ContractScrub, the first benchmark designed to evaluate contract scrubbing capabilities, comprising contracts hand-crafted by experienced lawyers over diverse error categories such as misuse of defined terms, incorrect references, and inconsistent language. Frontier models perform surprisingly poorly with only one model reaching 0.75 macro average recall despite strong performance on seemingly related general benchmarks, demonstrating the practical limits of current models and the importance of narrowly targeted, domain-specific benchmarks for measuring real-world impact.
2608.20204.paper_summary_zh: 法律工作因其對處理大量文本的高度依賴，常被認為是最容易受到大型語言模型（LLMs）影響的領域之一。合同“清理”，即對交易協議進行最終審查以查找錯誤和不一致性，是一項特別適合自動化的任務，因為這是一項常規且繁瑣的工作，需要對長文件進行詳細的關注。清理似乎也與前沿LLMs在長上下文推理、一致性檢查和命名實體識別（NER）方面的普遍能力自然對應。儘管具有經濟價值和自動化潛力，但尚未對執行合同清理的LLMs進行正式評估。我們介紹了ContractScrub，這是第一個旨在評估合同清理能力的基準，包含由經驗豐富的律師手工製作的合同，涵蓋了多種錯誤類別，例如定義術語的誤用、不正確的引用和不一致的語言。前沿模型的表現令人驚訝地差，只有一個模型達到了0.75的宏觀平均召回率，儘管在看似相關的一般基準上表現強勁，這顯示了當前模型的實際限制以及針對特定領域的狹窄目標基準在衡量現實世界影響方面的重要性。
